Rashi on Niddah 51a:10:1.hebrew: לענין מעשר - דהואיל ונמלך עליהן לאדם, הויא מחשבה וחייבין במעשר:
Rashi on Niddah 51a:10:1.english: With regard to tithes - That since he changed his mind concerning them [to use them] for human [consumption], it is [considered] intent, and they are obligated in tithes.

Rashi on Niddah 51a:10:2.english: Savory - [This is the Old French word] poliol, [meaning] pennyroyal.

Rashi on Niddah 51a:10:3.english: And the thyme - Savory [in Old French: sadreie].

Rashi on Niddah 51a:10:4.hebrew: נשמרין - ס"ד, אם היו נשמרין לאכילת אדם:
Rashi on Niddah 51a:10:4.english: Guarded - One might have thought [that it means]: If they were guarded for human consumption.

Rashi on Niddah 51a:11:1.hebrew: אלא לאו דזרען לבהמה וקתני - אם חזר ושמרן לאדם, חייבין:
Rashi on Niddah 51a:11:1.english: Rather, is it not that he planted them for an animal, and it teaches - If he subsequently guarded them for human [consumption], they are obligated [in tithes].

Rashi on Niddah 51a:12:1.hebrew: לאדם קיימי - וכיון דסתמייהו לאדם, מאי אם היו נשמרין? הכי קאמר: אם החצר משמרת פירותיה, דלא הוי הפקר — חייבין:
Rashi on Niddah 51a:12:1.english: They are intended for human [consumption] - And since by default they are for human [consumption], what is [the meaning of] "if they were guarded"? This is what it is saying: If the courtyard protects its produce, so that it is not ownerless, they are obligated [in tithes].

Rashi on Niddah 51a:13:1.english: Rav Ashi raises an objection - To Rava.

Rashi on Niddah 51a:13:2.hebrew: ואם איתא - דלענין מעשר הויא מחשבה, הא איכא עולשין שזרען לבהמה ונמלך עליהם לאדם, דחייבין במעשר ואינן מטמאין, דהא לענין טומאה אמרת לאו מחשבה היא:
Rashi on Niddah 51a:13:2.english: And if it is so - That with regard to tithes it is considered intent, behold, there are endives that one planted for animal [feed] and reconsidered concerning them for human [consumption], which are obligated in tithes and do not become impure, for with regard to ritual impurity you said that it is not considered intent.

Rashi on Niddah 51a:15:1.hebrew: ראשית הגז - הגוזז צאנו חייב ליתן בכל שנה מן הגז מעט לכהן, ובשחיטת חולין מפרש שיעורא:
Rashi on Niddah 51a:15:1.english: The first shearing - One who shears his flock is obligated each year to give a small amount of the sheared wool to a priest, and in [tractate] Shechitat Chullin, [the Gemara] explains the required amount.

Rashi on Niddah 51a:15:2.english: In the gifts - The foreleg, the jaw, and the maw.

Rashi on Niddah 51a:15:3.hebrew: ויש שחייב במתנות - כגון בקר, ואינו חייב בראשית הגז:
Rashi on Niddah 51a:15:3.english: And there is that which is subject to the gifts - Such as cattle, and it is not subject to the first shearing.

Rashi on Niddah 51a:18:1.english: Come and hear - That the mishna is teaching [categories of] species.

Rashi on Niddah 51a:18:2.hebrew: ופטור מן המעשר - דהפקר פטור מן המעשר. ובפרט ובפאה להכי מחייב, כדאמרינן בהגוזל בבבא קמא משום תעזוב יתירתא: דכתיב במשנה תורה לא תפאר אחריך, ואמר מר (חולין דף קלא.) לא תטול תפארתו ממנו — והיינו פאה, ודרשינן בספרי: אחריך — זו שכחה, וכתיב לגר ליתום ולאלמנה יהיה, וכתיב בתריה כי תבצור כרמך לא תעולל אחריך לגר ליתום ולאלמנה יהיה — הרי פאה ושכחה ועוללות. ל"ל למהדר ומכתב בפרשה קדושים בכולהו: לעני ולגר תעזוב אותם? לרבות הפקר כי האי גוונא. אבל הפקר גמור פטור מכולם, כדתנן לעיל: ונשמר — פרט להפקר:
Rashi on Niddah 51a:18:2.english: And he is exempt from tithes - For ownerless produce is exempt from tithes. And regarding peret and pe'ah, he is obligated for this [reason], as we say in [the chapter] HaGozel in Bava Kamma [94a], on account of the superfluous [word] "you shall leave" [ta'azov]: For it is written in Mishneh Torah [Deuteronomy 24:20]: "You shall not go over the boughs [lo tefa'er] after you," and the Master said (Chullin 131a): "Do not remove its splendor [tifarto] from it" — and that is pe'ah; and we expound in the Sifrei: "'After you' — this is shikhecha [forgotten produce]"; and it is written: "It shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow"; and it is written after it [verse 21]: "When you harvest your vineyard, you shall not glean [lo te'olel] after you; it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow" — behold, [we have] pe'ah, shikhecha, and olelot [already commanded]. Why did [the Torah] need to go back and write concerning all of them in the portion of Kedoshim [Leviticus 19:10]: "You shall leave them for the poor and for the stranger"? To include ownerless produce in a case like this. But completely ownerless produce is exempt from all of them, as we learned above: "And is protected" — to exclude ownerless produce.

Rashi on Niddah 51a:1:1.hebrew: טומאה חמורה אינה עושה כיוצא בה - מאחר שמטמאה נבלה את האדם, אין אותו אדם חוזר ומטמא אדם, שאין מטמא אדם אלא אב הטומאה. אבל אוכל חוזר ומטמא אוכל מדרבנן:
Rashi on Niddah 51a:1:1.english: Severe impurity does not produce its like - Since the carcass renders the person impure, that person does not in turn render [another] person impure, for nothing renders a person impure except a primary source of impurity. However, food does in turn render [other] food impure by rabbinic law.

Rashi on Niddah 51a:20:1.hebrew: תנן התם כו' - האי דנקט לה הכא, משום דאותיב עלה ממתני'. ודר' יוחנן נמי, עולשין שזרען כו' — משום דאותיב עליה ממתני' נקט לה הכא:
Rashi on Niddah 51a:20:1.english: We learned elsewhere, etc. - The reason that [the Gemara] cites it here is because it raises an objection against it from a mishna. And [the statement of] Rabbi Yoḥanan as well, "Endives that one planted, etc." — [the Gemara] cited it here because it raises an objection against him from a mishna.

Rashi on Niddah 51a:20:2.hebrew: מודים חכמים לרבי עקיבא - אע"פ דפליגי במנמר שדהו ושייר קלחים לחים. מנמר - טיי"ר בלע"ז, שמלקט כאן את המבושלים כל צרכן, ומניח את הלחים שלא בשלו, וחוזר ומלקט במקום אחר, דהוה ליה מנומר. וקאמר ר' עקיבא: כשהוא חוזר ולוקט, נותן פאה מכל אחד ואחד, שהקציר שבינתים מפסיק; וחכמים אומרים: פאה מאחת על הכל. ומודים חכמים לרבי עקיבא בזורע שבת או חרדל כו' - להכי נקט הני, שאין דרכן לעשות מהן ערוגה, אלא זורען לתבלין בעלמא בשנים ושלשה מקומות. שבת - אני"ט:
Rashi on Niddah 51a:20:2.english: The Sages concede to Rabbi Akiva - [They concede here,] even though they disagree in [the case of] one who harvests his field in patches and leaves moist stalks. Menamer [teier in Old French, meaning patchy or spotted] is where one gathers here those [stalks] that are fully ripe, and leaves the moist ones that have not ripened, and goes and gathers in another place, so that it [the field] becomes patchy. And Rabbi Akiva says: When he goes back and gathers [the remaining stalks], he gives pe'ah from each and every one, because the harvesting [done] in the interim divides [them]; and the Sages say: [He gives] pe'ah from one [patch] for all [of them]. [And the mishna continues:] "And the Sages concede to Rabbi Akiva in [the case of] one who sows dill or mustard, etc." - It specifically mentioned these [species] because it is not the practice to make a [whole] bed of them; rather, one sows them merely for seasoning in two or three places. Shevet is anit [dill] in Old French.

Rashi on Niddah 51a:5:1.english: Preparation of a creeping animal - That they prepare a creeping animal, to bring it to ritual impurity.

Rashi on Niddah 51a:8:1.english: Which will not ultimately transmit severe impurity - There is no food that defiles a person.

Rashi on Niddah 51a:9:1.hebrew: שום טומאה חמורה שום טומאה קלה - לא, אם אמרת בטומאה חמורה, דין הוא שמטמא בלא מחשבה, שלא מצינו שום טומאה ששמה טומאה חמורה שתהא צריכה הכשר; תאמר בטומאה קלה דאוכלין, שאע"פ שזו אינה צריכה הכשר — הרי כל אוכלין יש עליהם שום טומאה קלה וצריכין הכשר, הלכך הכא נמי בעיא מחשבה:
Rashi on Niddah 51a:9:1.english: The designation of severe impurity, the designation of lenient impurity - No; if you said [this] regarding severe impurity, it is logical that it transmits impurity without intention, as we do not find any impurity whose designation is severe impurity that requires preparation [by liquid]. Shall you say [so] regarding the lenient impurity of food? For even though this [carcass] does not require preparation [by liquid], all foods bear the designation of lenient impurity and require preparation [by liquid]; therefore, here too, it requires intention.

Tosafot on Niddah 51a:11:1.hebrew: אלא דזרעינהו לבהמה - והא דנקט שבחצר, לפי מאי דמסיק שעלו מאיליהן, אתי שפיר: משום דבחצר אין דרך לזרוע אלא בגינה; ועוד, דבחצר סתמא לאדם, לפי שרואה ויודע מתי ללוקטן עד שלא יתקשו. ולפי מאי דס"ד השתא, יש לפרש דנקט חצר לפי שדרך התנא למנקט חצר, דגם בשאר דבר תני חצר; דקתני התם: תאנה עומדת בחצר אוכל אחת מהן ופטור ואם צירף חייב, גפן נטוע בחצר, כקורנית שבחצר — שהחצר קובעת בדבר שנגמרה מלאכתו אם צירף, או בלא צירוף כהנהו שאין רגילין לעשות מהן גורן. והא דתנן פ"ח דשביעית [מ"א]: כל שאינו מיוחד לא לאוכל אדם ולא לאוכל בהמה, חישב עליו לאוכל אדם ולאוכל בהמה נותנין חומרי אדם וחומרי בהמה, כגון האזוב והקורנית — לא קשה אהא דאמרינן בשמעתין דסתמיה לאדם; דהיינו דוקא בחצר, כדפרישית לעיל:
Tosafot on Niddah 51a:11:1.english: Rather, that he sowed them for animals - And that which [the mishna] specified, "which are in a courtyard," according to that which [the Gemara] concludes, that they grew on their own, works out well: because in a courtyard it is not the usual practice to sow, but rather in a garden; and furthermore, in a courtyard, [their] default status is for human [consumption], because [the owner] sees [them] and knows when to harvest them before they harden. And according to what enters our mind now [in the Gemara's initial assumption], it can be explained that [the Tanna] specified "a courtyard" because it is the way of the Tanna to specify "a courtyard," for regarding other matters as well he teaches "a courtyard"; as it teaches there: "A fig tree that stands in a courtyard, one may eat one of them and is exempt [from tithes], but if he combined [them], he is liable"; "[A] vine planted in a courtyard..."; [and so too,] like thyme in a courtyard — for a courtyard establishes [liability for tithes] in an item whose processing is completed if he combined [them], or [even] without combination, in the case of those [items] for which it is not customary to make a threshing floor. And that which we learned [in a mishna] in chapter 8 of Shevi'it [Mishnah 1]: "Anything that is not specifically designated either for human food or for animal food, [if] one designated it for human food and for animal food, we apply to it the stringencies of [food for] humans and the stringencies of [food for] animals, such as hyssop and thyme" — this is not difficult with respect to that which we say in our sugya, that unspecified [produce of this type] is [presumed to be] for human [consumption]; for that is specifically in a courtyard, as I explained above.

Tosafot on Niddah 51a:19:1.hebrew: מין קתני ש"מ - וא"ת: בריש הגוזל קמא (ב"ק צד.) קאמר אביי דלר' ישמעאל שינוי אין קונה, דקאמרי רבנן לא הפריש פאה מן הקמה יפריש מן העמרים או מן הכרי ולא מן העיסה, ולר"ש אף מן העיסה. ודחי רבא: בעלמא שינוי קונה, והכא משום תעזוב יתירא. ואביי: תעזוב יתירא למפקיר כרמו. אם כן, לרבא, מפקיר כרמו פטור מן הפאה לר"ש; וא"כ, היכי מוכח הכא דמין קתני? דילמא מתני' דקתני כל שחייב בפאה חייב במעשר, ר"ש היא! וי"ל, דלרבא נמי תעזוב יתירא למפקיר כרמו, ותרתי ש"מ. דהא אביי נמי, דדריש ליה בהגוזל קמא (שם צד.) למפקיר כרמו לכ"ע, דריש לה בפ"ק דתמורה (דף ו.) למילתא אחריתי, דקאמר התם אביי: כל דאמר רחמנא לא תעביד אי עביד מהני ליה. מותיב רבא: והרי פאה, דאמר רחמנא לא תכלה, ואמרינן דאם לא הפריש מן הקמה יפריש מן העומרין או מן הכרי לרבנן או אף מן העיסה לר"ש, אלמא דלא מהני! ומשני אביי התם: משום תעזוב יתירא. ורבא: תעזוב יתירא למפקיר כרמו. והשתא, בין אביי ובין רבא דרשי תעזוב למפקיר כרמו. ואביי, דסבר דבעלמא אי עביד מהני, דריש נמי מתעזוב דיפריש מן העומרים או מן הכרי או מעיסה לר"ש, דלא נימא אי עביד מהני. אבל אי בעלמא שינוי קונה לר"ש כמו בגזל, אין סברא להעמיד תעזוב שיפריש מן העיסה, אלא דדוקא מעמרים או מהכרי. ורבא סבר דתעזוב למפקיר כרמו, ולר' שמעון שיפריש מן העיסה אע"ג דבעלמא שינוי קונה; אבל להפריש מן העומרים או מן הכרי לא צריך קרא, דבעלמא נמי כל דאמר רחמנא לא תעביד אי עביד לא מהני לרבא:
Tosafot on Niddah 51a:19:1.english: [The mishna] teaches [general] types; conclude from it - And if you say: At the beginning of [the chapter] HaGozel Kama (Bava Kamma 94a), Abaye states that according to Rabbi Yishmael, a change does not acquire [ownership of a transformed item], as the Rabbis say: [If] one did not separate pe'ah from the standing grain, he separates [it] from the sheaves or from the pile, but not from the dough; and according to Rabbi Shimon, [he separates] even from the dough. And Rava rejects [this: In fact,] in general a change acquires [ownership], and here [the obligation to give from dough] is because of the superfluous [verse], "you shall leave" (Leviticus 19:10). And Abaye [maintains that] the superfluous "you shall leave" is [needed] for one who declares his vineyard ownerless [to obligate him in pe'ah]. If so, according to Rava, one who declares his vineyard ownerless is exempt from pe'ah according to Rabbi Shimon; and if so, how is it proven here that [the mishna] teaches [general] types? Perhaps the mishna, which teaches: "Whatever is liable in pe'ah is liable in tithes," is [the view of] Rabbi Shimon [and according to him, one who declares his vineyard ownerless is exempt from both pe'ah and tithes, so there is no exception to the mishna's rule]! And one can answer that according to Rava as well, the superfluous "you shall leave" is [used] for one who declares his vineyard ownerless, and two [halakhot] are derived from it. For indeed Abaye as well, who in HaGozel Kama (ibid. 94a) derives it for one who declares his vineyard ownerless according to everyone, derives it in the first chapter of Temurah (6a) for another matter: as Abaye states there, [regarding] anything that the Merciful One said "Do not do," if one did [it], it takes effect. Rava objects: But there is pe'ah, where the Merciful One said "You shall not wholly reap" (Leviticus 23:22), and we say that if one did not separate from the standing grain, he separates from the sheaves or from the pile according to the Rabbis, or even from the dough according to Rabbi Shimon — thus [proving] that it does not take effect! And Abaye answers there: [It is different there] because of the superfluous "you shall leave." And Rava [retorts]: The superfluous "you shall leave" is [needed] for one who declares his vineyard ownerless. And now, both Abaye and Rava derive [from] "you shall leave" [the obligation of] one who declares his vineyard ownerless. And Abaye, who holds that in general if one did [what was prohibited] it takes effect, also derives from "you shall leave" that he must separate from the sheaves or from the pile, or from dough according to Rabbi Shimon, so that we should not say that if one did [transgress], it takes effect. However, if in general a change acquires [ownership] according to Rabbi Shimon, as in [the case of] robbery, there is no reason to establish "you shall leave" [as teaching] that he separates from dough, but rather specifically from sheaves or from the pile. And Rava holds that "you shall leave" is [derived both] for one who declares his vineyard ownerless, and, according to Rabbi Shimon, that he must separate from dough even though in general a change acquires [ownership]; but to separate from the sheaves or from the pile, no verse is needed, since in general as well, [regarding] anything that the Merciful One said "Do not do," if one did [it], it does not take effect, according to Rava:

Tosafot on Niddah 51a:9:1.hebrew: שום טומאה חמורה בעולם כו' - תימה, דיפרש הא דקתני דאינה יורדת לכך, המחשבה גופה; דלא מצינו טומאה חמורה שצריכה מחשבה בשום מקום. דהא דאמרינן דנבלת בהמה ועוף טהור צריכין מחשבה, היינו לטומאת אוכלין, לצרף פחות מכזית ופחות מכביצה אוכלין; אבל כזית מהם מטמא אדם וכלים בלא מחשבה, כדפרישית. אבל טומאה קלה צריכה מחשבה בעלמא. ומיהו, נבלה נמי בעינן שתהא ראויה לגר, לבר פדא:
Tosafot on Niddah 51a:9:1.english: Any severe impurity in the world, etc. - It is puzzling: let [the Gemara] explain that which [the Baraita] teaches, "that it does not descend into this," [as referring to] the thought itself, for we do not find severe impurity that requires thought anywhere. For that which we say that the carcass of an animal and of a kosher bird require thought — that is [only] with regard to the impurity of food, to combine less than an olive-bulk [of carcass] and less than an egg-bulk of [other] food; but an olive-bulk of them transmits impurity to people and vessels without thought, as I have explained. Whereas lenient impurity requires thought in general. However, regarding a carcass, we also require that it be fit for a stranger (ger), according to Bar Pada.
